Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Scope: `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution-calldata-relation-disabled-package-35526.test.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.relation-condition-target-exposure.test.ts`, `.changeset/36393-calldata-disabled-package-every-hop.md`, `.changeset/35526-calldata-relation-disabled-package.md`, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` (row 48) + cited, read only: `packages/core/src/utils/relation-condition-sites.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/relation-filter-lowering.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-query-lowering.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry-package-addressing.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md`, `contract-review.md`, `landing-operations.md`

Head note. The review was asked at `d6f70d698c`. The head moved twice during the review. I read both deltas.
- `d6f70d698c` to `af5e5f8e10`: one line in `.changeset/36393-calldata-disabled-package-every-hop.md`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing…)` to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing…)`. No code.
- `af5e5f8e10` to `9198e1cd47`: `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` drops the `context?.isSystem` early return in the relation walk and rewords its comment; `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 48 gains one sentence. Nothing else.
This record is for `9198e1cd47`. Merge base: `6a731859de`. Everything below is read from the diff and the tree. Nothing was run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Every hop, callData: yes.** `refuseUnservedRelationTargets` is now a recursive `walk(schema, condition, prefix, depth)`. At each site it asks the package predicate, then resolves the target, then asks exposure (when `exposureGated`), then descends into `site.condition` against the target's field map. `param` is the full position (`where.c_ref.b2_ref`). Both arms that hand the engine a caller's `where` call it: the `aggregate` arm and the no-protocol `query` fallback. The query arm on a protocol host goes through `findData`, which already asks every hop.

**Every hop, stdio bridge: yes.** `enforceRelationTargetExposure` recurses the same way. Each target gets the whole of `enforceApiExposure` (the by-name read throws the package refusal first, then exposure) at its full position. Both call sites (`query`, `aggregate`) pass through it.

**`$or`, `$and`, `$not`, nested: covered.** Both walks find sites with `relationConditionSites`, which walks every `$` key and every array member. Inside a relation condition the engine admits declared field keys only (`admitRelationCondition` refuses an undeclared key), so a combinator beneath a lookup is refused by the engine before any read. The walk still looks there. The walk's site set is a superset of what the engine lowers.

**Bounded and cycle-safe: yes.** Depth stops past `RELATION_CONDITION_WALK_DEPTH = 8`, the same number as the protocol's twin walk and the engine's evaluate gate. The engine serves `RELATION_CONDITION_MAX_HOPS = 3`, so the walk asks at least every hop the engine serves. `relationConditionSites` holds a `WeakSet` per call, so a cycle inside one level ends. A cycle across levels ends at depth 8. A condition past three hops is refused by the engine (`hop-limit`) at admission, before any related read.

**System caller: exactly the ruling.** The package question left the `exposureGated` guard. It is asked of every caller, for the addressed object (top of `callData`, every action) and for every relation target. The exposure question still sits under `asked.exposureGated` and `refuseUnexposedDataAction` still returns early for system. A pin holds that a system context is served a two-hop condition into an unexposed object.

**Stdio bridge system behaviour: unchanged, and it does not ask the package question.** At this head the walk has no `isSystem` branch of its own. It runs for a system context, and at every hop it calls `enforceApiExposure`, whose first line returns for `isSystem` before it reads the declaration. The package refusal on this bridge lives in that by-name read, so a system context is asked neither question at any hop. The walk's own field-map read catches a thrown package refusal and finds no site; it refuses nothing. So the answer for system is the one `main` gives. The only difference from `af5e5f8e10` is that the walk now does its field-map reads for a system caller too, as `main` did at the first hop. The pin "a system context is not asked the exposure question at any hop" still holds. Dropping the branch is right: one owner for the bypass, and the census counts one site.

**Should stdio match the ruling? Not in this PR.** The ruling's words bind `callData`. The reason behind it (a disabled package is off the data plane for every caller, as the protocol answers) applies to the stdio bridge as well, so I expect the same answer there. But it is a second published door with its own host population, and nobody has ruled on it. It does not match today. See ④, note N2.

**Doc sentence, row 48: true of the code.** "The bypass covers exposure only: a disabled package's object is refused `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` to a system context too, addressed or as a relation target at any hop". The row is the runtime row (`callData`, `refuseUnexposedDataAction`). In `callData` the addressed-object check runs for every caller on every action, and the relation walk asks the package predicate for every caller at every hop. Exposure stays skipped for system. The sentence does not speak for the stdio bridge, which has its own row 15. Prose face, so outside the L2 face, but it is checked here because the PR adds it.

**No-protocol host, addressed object: closed and measured.** `packageDisabledPredicate` reads the engine registry's `isObjectPackageDisabled` once per call (`getObjectQL`, then the `objectql` slot) and `callData` throws `objectPackageDisabledError(params.object)` before any exposure verdict. The predicate resolves names (`resolveObjectKey`), as the data route's does. The PR body states the before-fix measurement. Eight pins hold it: `aggregate` and `query`, member and system, both hosts, each with a real re-enable control.

**Clause-② line.** The repo defines the value by one question: does the card widen the accepted set or enlarge the public surface (`execution-duties.md` line 76; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`). A card that narrows a published accepted set is `Clause-②: no` (`execution-duties.md` line 108). A runtime security change is not Clause-② (line 106). `yes (narrowing)` is defined as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another". This diff adds no export and widens nothing. So the true line is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The first spelling on this branch was the true one. The line at this head, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, copies the claim (7099212652), as the SKILL.md template tells the dev to do. It over-declares. I grade this a note, not a fix, for three reasons. The over-declaration is in the safe direction (a wrong `no` is the auditable false declaration, `landing-operations.md` line 8). Every gate reads `yes (narrowing)` and `no (narrowing)` as the same narrowing face at the same tier. And the claim, the PR body and the changeset agree at this head. If the seat wants the true value, it amends the claim to `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` first, then the PR body and the changeset in one stroke. A PR line that disagrees with the claim would be worse than either spelling.

**Metadata-protocol line.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is true. No key, accepted value or metadata type moves.

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/35526-calldata-relation-disabled-package.md`.** Three lines changed. The frontmatter did not.

Line 1, OLD: "Clause-②: no (narrowing: for a non-system caller, `callData`'s `aggregate` arm and its `query` fallback on a host with no protocol service refuse a nested-relation condition whose target belongs to a disabled package with 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, where they answered the count or the matching rows)"
Line 1, NEW: "Clause-②: yes (narrowing: adds the root export `objectPackageDisabledError` to `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`; for a non-system caller, `callData`'s `aggregate` arm and its `query` fallback on a host with no protocol service refuse a nested-relation condition whose target belongs to a disabled package with 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, where they answered the count or the matching rows)"
Correct. #36337 added that root export (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` line 14). A new export enlarges the public surface, so `yes` is true here. This is what #36393 item 3 asks.

Line 2, OLD: "- TO: the call is refused `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, naming the disabled object as `object` and the condition's position as `param` (for example `where.b_ref`), before the engine reads anything. The error is the data route's own."
Line 2, NEW: "- TO: a condition directly beneath a lookup of the queried object is refused `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, naming the disabled object as `object` and the condition's position as `param` (for example `where.b_ref`), before the engine reads anything. The error is the data route's own."
Correct. It uses the card's own words. #36337 refused one hop only.

Line 3, OLD: "The fix: re-enable the package to filter on its records again, or filter on the lookup's stored id. An environment with no disabled package sees no change. A system context (an in-process caller, such as a hook's `ctx.api`) is not changed: it is still answered the count."
Line 3, NEW: "The fix: re-enable the package to filter on its records again, or filter on the lookup's stored id. An environment with no disabled package sees no change. A system context handed to `callData` is not changed by this entry: it is still answered the count. (A hook's `ctx.api` is not such a caller: it reaches the engine directly and never passes through `callData`.)"
Correct. The false gloss is gone. "by this entry" keeps the sentence true beside the new entry, which refuses system.

Not consumed: the file is on `origin/main`, no `CHANGELOG.md` on `origin/main` carries its text, and the version PR #35129 is open and unmerged. So the changeset is the right place, not a CHANGELOG. **This correction is intended and correct.** `check:empty-changeset` is red on it by design. This same-head record at the contract-review tier is the confirmation `landing-operations.md` asks for.

### ② Semver level

- The new changeset grades `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp` `patch`. Those are the two packages whose published source moves. Both are graded. No `major`.
- `patch` is right. AGENTS.md step 3: a non-protocol change, breaking or not, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`.
- The title's `!` is right for a narrowing. The changeset carries the **BREAKING** banner, FROM and TO, the one-line fix, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).
- The corrected #35526 changeset keeps its levels (`runtime` and `metadata-protocol`, `patch`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Order: disabled before unexposed, and pinned.** In the walk the package throw comes before the exposure check. At the top of `callData` the package throw comes before `refuseUnexposedDataAction`. Pins: a relation target both disabled and `apiEnabled: false` (both hosts), the addressed object both ways (both hosts), and the stdio twin for `query` and `aggregate`. Each relation pin then re-enables and expects the exposure refusal.
- **Error shape: the data route's.** `objectPackageDisabledError` is the protocol's one constructor. Pins compare `code`, `status` 404, `object` and `param`.
- **Remaining 1/0 oracles: none found on this door.** Aggregate and count: refused before `engine.aggregate`. An aggregation's own `filter` and `having`: the engine lowers relation conditions in `where` only (`resolveWhereTokens`; the per-aggregation filter takes `resolveThenLowerWhere` with no relation step). Query arms: the protocol path asks every hop; the fallback is walked. Deeper than three hops: the engine refuses at admission. Reverse relation: not served by the engine. `master_detail`, `user`, `tree`: the walk and the engine share `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` and `referenceTargetOf`.
- **Re-enable control: real.** Every control calls `disablePackage` and then `enablePackage`. The old query-fallback control that never disabled now does (N1).
- **No test weakened.** The 16 removed lines are the old header text and the one SYSTEM pin that held "the count is served". That pin flips to refused, as the ruling orders, and gains a control. No assertion was loosened.
- **Pins fail without the fix: consistent by reading.** I counted the runtime pins that the main source cannot pass: 12 two-hop aggregate, 6 addressed-object, 3 query-fallback, 2 flipped SYSTEM. That is 23, the thread's number. Stdio: two verbs times five (three shapes, package, order) is 10. Read, not run.
- **Fail-open kept, not widened.** A target schema that cannot be resolved finds no deeper site. The package predicate is asked by name before the schema is read, so a disabled target is refused even then.

### ④ Design judgment

The change does what card #36393 items 1 to 3 and ruling 7077381587 ask, and no more. One walk per door, the same order as the protocol's twin, the protocol's own error, one predicate read per call. Using the engine registry for the predicate is the right fix for the no-protocol host: the refusal no longer depends on a service the host may not register.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Notes:
- N1. Clause-② value. The true line under the written definition is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The head carries `yes (narrowing)` to match the claim. Safe direction, same face, same tier. If corrected, correct the claim first and then all three places together.
- N2. Not in scope and not filed: the stdio bridge on a no-protocol host still serves a disabled package's object, and a system principal on the stdio bridge is asked neither question at any hop. The ruling names `callData` only, so the PR is right to leave both. The seat should file one card so the question reaches the maintainer. Row 15 of the system-context page says only that the bridge skips the exposure gate; that card can fix the row too. It is not this PR's to decide.
- N3. The PR body has a `(narrowing)` arm and no `Skills-docs:` line. The SKILL.md template owes one. This is the seat's L1 line, with no head move.
- N4. The title's `!` owes the dogfood battery. The PR body still reports it as running at `af5e5f8e10`, and its Verification section names older heads. The seat's L1 needs both restated for `9198e1cd47`.
- N5. No three-hop pin. The recursion is generic and two hops prove the descent. A three-hop pin at the engine's limit would be cheap.
- N6. "No door in this repository hands `callData` a system context" rests on the ruling's analysis. I spot-read `action-dispatch.ts`: its `callData` calls carry the request's own context. I did not re-audit every caller.
- N7. The walk reads `where` in object form only. The PR body says so. The engine's relation lowering reads the same form.
- N8. `packageDisabledPredicate` adds one engine resolution to every `callData` call. Small, and worth knowing.
